column1: # Every mechanism that keeps a produced finding out of the published report, and
# what each one records today. The step's machine-readable surface generalises
# over this set, so the set is enumerated rather than described.
# HOW THIS WAS PRODUCED
# - Rows 1-6 are the closed vocabularies themselves, not a grep over their uses:
#   `FindingFilterStage`'s five cases (src/Analysis/Finding/Contract/Filter/FindingFilterStage.php)
#   plus the per-rule ledger, which runs earlier and therefore is not a stage
#   (src/Analysis/Finding/FindingExclusionLedger.php, reported separately by
#   FindingFilterOrchestrator::reportRuleExclusions()).
# - Rows 7-11 are the neighbouring mechanisms that also make a finding invisible
#   and are NOT suppression; they are listed so the surface's scope is a decision
#   rather than an omission. Rows 10 and 11 were missing from the first revision:
#   the claim in this file's own title is "every mechanism", and a review found
#   two the enum-plus-ledger method cannot see, because neither is a filter stage
#   and neither runs inside rule execution.
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
# - A future stage added outside the enum: FindingFilterStage's own docblock makes
#   that a declaration error, so the blind spot is closed by the product, not here.
# - Suppression a rule performs internally before emitting (a rule that decides not
#   to produce a finding at all). By construction nothing downstream can observe it;
#   `@qmx-threshold` is exactly that case, which is why the threshold audit is the
#   other half of this step.
# - A configured suppressor that never matched anything. It produces no row of
#   "mechanism x finding" at all, so in a composition keyed on what fired it is
#   indistinguishable from a suppressor that does not exist. Four live examples
#   in this repository: `exclude_paths` entries in qmx.yaml naming files that no
#   longer exist. The step publishes them as their own block for that reason.

per-rule exclude_namespaces / exclude_namespace_channels / exclude_paths
